outreach/pipeline.md:34:- Irrigation & sprinkler (batch 1, 11 candidates, 2026-09-09): new segment. Mid-September is the ramp-up to Denver's winterization season (average first hard freeze around October 8, blowout window roughly late September through mid-November); multiple shops warn October appointments fill fast. Pricing observed on company sites runs $85 flat (Mile Hi Services, multi-trade, excluded) to $150 per blowout (Sprinkler Doctor), a high-margin, high-volume, short-window service. Shops skew heavily owner-operator or small family crews (Conrad Olivier at 5280 Sprinklers, Hawkins Brothers, Dave Ferdon's Thornton Sprinklers) who answer their own phones while in the field, the perfect missed-call pain profile: a homeowner who gets voicemail during a freeze warning books the next name on the list, and the shop loses both the blowout and the spring startup. Several shops already push text-first or online booking (303 Sprinklers, 5280 Sprinklers, Sprinkler Doctor), signaling they feel inbound strain. Skip patterns logged: national franchises (Conserva Irrigation), multi-trade companies where blowouts are a side offering (Mile Hi Services, Omni Landscape, Denver Lawn & Snow Care), fire-suppression sprinkler companies (Denver Fire Pro), and directory-only operations with no real site (Gorman's Sprinklers Too, KHEN Sprinklers). Verification caveats kept: Thornton "Sprinklers" (Dave Ferdon) dropped entirely, no own site found; Preferred Sprinklers recorded as form-route only since its directory phone never appeared on its own site.
outreach/pipeline.md:40:- Handyman (Western CO, 4 candidates, 2026-09-09): fall is the busiest booking window: honey-do lists, deck/fence repairs, gutter cleaning, swamp-cooler winterization before the first hard freeze, heat-cable and pipe protection, holiday-guest prep punch lists. Second-home owners in Aspen/Snowmass/Steamboat send photo-based requests from out of town. Core pain: missed calls and slow estimates while the owner is on a ladder, plus estimate follow-up that dies when the day runs long; photo intake and estimate-chasing are the fit. Market is heavy with phone-only operators, directory-only listings, and dead sites; only own sites with a real email or form qualified.
outreach/pipeline.md:44:- Plumbing (Western Colorado, batch 13, 2026-09-09): new segment, 2 verified candidates. Shops are overwhelmingly phone-first; smaller independents rarely publish an email or form on their own sites, so the strict own-site rule throttled yield. Mid-September 2026 is shoulder season: irrigation/swamp-cooler work winding down, boiler and heating service about to ramp, second-home and short-term-rental turnover steady in resort markets. Regional players in Montrose and Grand Junction skew family-owned multi-tech with 15-30 years of history; Cortez, Gunnison, Craig, Meeker run thinner with owner-operators.
outreach/pipeline.md:47:- Instagram Western CO (9 prospects, 2026-09-10): plumbing, landscape/irrigation, remodel, multi-trade, tree care, and HVAC shops in GJ, Montrose, Durango, Rifle, and Gypsum all publishing emails in bios; all drafted into tailored emails and QUEUED. Notable: James Cook (VIP Plumbing, Durango) is a second-generation Colorado Certified Master Plumber running BlueLight trenchless pipe lining with 24-7 emergency; Littell Electric (Glenwood) is a high-end residential/automation shop where project qualification matters as much as speed.
outreach/pipeline.md:52:- Snow removal (Western Colorado, batch 15, 2026-09-10): new segment, 5 verified candidates. Mid-September lands squarely in the snow contract-signing window (September through November), the segment's highest-intent inbound period. Own-site evidence documents storm cleanups starting 2-3am with 14-16 hour storm days; storm-morning call chaos, route-capacity pressure, early-hour dispatch, and seasonal contract renewals are the missed-call pain PING targets. Commercial operators with multi-crew routes (D&D Asphalt, Summit Sweeping, Grasshoppers) are the strongest fits. Thinner than expected under the own-site rule; mostly landscaping/asphalt hybrids, phone-primary. If the pool thins, revisit phone-primary near-misses (Peaceful Valley, J&J Snow Removal) or Facebook engagement.
outreach/pipeline.md:54:- Electrical (Western Colorado, batch 17, 2026-09-10): new segment, 6 verified candidates. September is the pre-heating and pre-winter reliability window: generator evaluations, panel upgrades, service calls, second-home winterization, lighting and shade automation projects, and 24/7 emergency positioning all peak at once. Resort and mountain shops (Steamboat, Glenwood Springs, Durango, Bayfield) sell high-end residential and automation work where qualification and routing matter more than raw lead volume. Owner-led field work with phone/form intake is the norm; pitch reliable capture while electricians are on jobs, not replacing technical judgment. Skip patterns: lead-broker style "electrical network" sites (Duft/Colorado Electrical Network), generic SEO-location pages, and larger multi-tech firms that dilute the owner-led fit (R&A Enterprises included with a size caveat).
outreach/pipeline.md:65:- Insulation (Western Colorado, research batch round 25, 2026-09-11): new segment, 1 qualified (Eagle Insulation, Durango, robert@eagleinsulationco.com). Pool is genuinely thin under the own-site rule: 11 near-misses logged, most established GJ firms are phone-only own sites or directory-only. Durango/Pagosa spray foam scene is tied to mountain-town winterization and second-home work; 4CORE preferred-contractor list is the pressure point (rebate and energy-efficiency questions create qualification load). Seasonal timing favorable (mid-September pre-heating-season weatherization rush). Pitch: field-heavy crews publish same-day or 24-hour callback promises; instant-response lead capture is the concrete angle. Expect future insulation batches to stay small.
outreach/pipeline.md:77:- Landscapers / lawn care (Mesa County corridor, round 100, 2026-09-20): 7 qualified, corridor towns only. Segment heat is high RIGHT NOW: fall cleanup + aeration/overseeding are at peak inbound, and the aeration booking window is only 4-6 weeks, so a missed call is a permanently lost slot. Snow contract sign-ups run Sept-Nov (scheduling discipline and fast follow-up win them); irrigation winterization/blowouts are the October-November second wave. Owner-as-receptionist is the dominant pattern: nearly every independent is phone-only or form-only with no email or booking widget, making missed-call lead capture the highest-fit angle. Yardbook adoption is real among small lawn shops (Boyd's, Rock N Roots rent their whole web presence to the platform), which makes the owned-site + direct-capture pitch credible. Fruita/Clifton hold a large directory-only untapped pool that stays near-miss until an own site or real FB Page surfaces. Email-route yield was 0 of 7 under the strict own-site rule (Rock N Roots' email is Yardbook/directory-sourced, kept NEW unverified). Strongest phone-route candidate: Beard and Blade Greenworks (Fruita), aeration/overseeding headline service, peak season is literally now.

Chain/dealer captured: Groundworks (acquired Foundation Repair of Western Colorado), Supportworks dealer (Aspen Foundation Repairs, already WATCH), Basement Systems dealers (Silver River, Colorado Crawl Space), Pueblo-regional (Colorado Structural Repair). One independent WATCH: Tom Peters / "Colorado Foundation Repair" (Fruita, phone-only, no genuine own site; coloradofoundationrepair.com is a Front Range SEO lead-farm). Segment is project/estimate-driven, so missed-call fit is WEAKER than emergency trades; angle is free-estimate lead capture while crews are on job sites. Seasonal why-now: monsoon + summer irrigation swelling expansive soils, pre-freeze inspection season.
